scope: the id loop is a clean 12-bit read per entity, yet the position advanced by 20 - so the N-bit reader 0x66EC30 advances more than N

the_loop_0x6716a1.0x6716A1: push 0xC ; mov eax,esi ; call 0x66EC30   -> read 12 bits
the_loop_0x6716a1.0x6716AD: mov word [ecx*2 + 0x7859358], ax          -> store the id
the_loop_0x6716a1.0x6716BF: cmp bl,al ; jb 0x6716A1                   -> loop exactly count times
the_loop_0x6716a1.0x6716C3: pop ebx ; then compare al,1 and either set [0x7859559] = 0 or compute a width and return 1

the_reader_0x66ec30.0x66EC3E: cmp ebx,0x20 ; je 0x66ED43    - a 32-bit special case exists
the_reader_0x66ec30.0x66EC6F: ecx = [esi+0x20] >> 3          - the byte index is derived FROM the bit position
the_reader_0x66ec30.0x66EC75: cmp ecx,edi ; jl 0x66EC8D      - bounds check against the length
the_reader_0x66ec30.conclusion: it reads N bits starting at bit position [+0x20], using the byte index and the bit offset within it

the_measurement_that_needs_explaining: bitpos at 0x67169D (just after the count store) was 1309
the loop reads 12 bits exactly once
so the position advanced by 20 for a 12-bit read
either the reader rounds the advance up in some way, or an extra read happens inside the loop that the disassembly of 0x6716A1..0x6716C1 does not show
the_single_probe_that_settles_it: log [+0x20] at 0x6716A5 (the instruction right after the id read returns) and at 0x6716C3
the difference is exactly what one 12-bit read costs in position units, which is the unit every subsequent payload calculation depends on
why_this_matters_for_the_payload: the per-entity payload starts right after the id, and its field table 0xDA63E8 is indexed by 0x58-byte struct offsets
knowing the exact unit the position advances in is the prerequisite for computing where the first payload field begins
